Question: How can high-entropy materials (HEMs) leverage configurational entropy to overcome the limitations of conventional enthalpy-dominated catalysts, specifically regarding phase stability, active site tunability, and the breaking of scaling relationships in electrocatalysis?. System: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) including PtPdCoNiFeCuAuSn, PtPdRhRuCe, Ru0.44Rh0.30Co0.12Ni0.14, CoxMoyFe10Ni10Cu10, IrPdPtRhRu, Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, and AlNiCoIrM; High-entropy oxides (HEOs) and perovskites; Multimetallic nanoclusters (MMNCs).. Processing: Carbothermal shock (ultrafast joule heating followed by rapid quenching at ~1500 K); Fast moving bed pyrolysis (FMBP) reaching 923 K within 5 s; Colloidal synthesis with seed-mediated coreduction and annealing at 600°C; Ionic liquid-assisted cosputtering; Ball milling and solvothermal synthesis.. Test conditions: Ammonia oxidation at 700°C; Ammonia decomposition at 500°C; Oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in acidic and alkaline media; Oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in acidic and alkaline media; Hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic and alkaline solutions; Li-O2 battery cycling.. Findings: Quinary HEA nanoparticles (PtPdRhRuCe) achieved ~100% conversion and >99% selectivity toward NO + NO2 at 700°C with no degradation over 30 hours.; HEA-Co25Mo45 catalyst reached a mass-specific rate of 0.74 gNH3 m−2 hour−1 at 500°C, representing improvement factors of ~24 versus bimetallic Co-Mo and ~19 versus Ru.; Computational models predicted an IrPdPtRhRu HEA composition with a ~40-mV lower overpotential relative to Pt (111) for ORR.; Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni nanoparticles with size less than 2 nm delivered ORR activity comparable to Pt under the same conditions.; Octonary RuIrCeNiWCuCrCo catalyst outperformed quaternary and binary counterparts in long-term operation for Li-O2 batteries due to higher configurational entropy.; GO-supported quinary HEA nanoparticles (FeCoPdIrPt) exhibited enhanced HER activity and stability in alkaline solutions relative to commercial Pt/C catalysts.; HEA catalysts containing five or more elements outperformed binary, ternary, and quaternary alloys in alkaline media due to broad adsorption energy distributions.. Mechanism: Enhanced configurational entropy stabilizes single-phase solid solutions despite large enthalpic differences, allowing atomic mixing of multiple principal elements. Severe lattice distortion lowers the energy barrier for adsorption and activation, while the diverse local coordination environments and electronic perturbations (ligand effects) create a near-continuum distribution of adsorption energies. This distribution allows the catalyst to access optimal binding strengths for intermediates, breaking the linear scaling relationships that limit conventional catalysts.. Limitations: Low surface area of bulk HEAs limits catalytic utilization; maintaining nanoscale morphology at elevated temperatures is difficult due to migration and aggregation; synthesis of single-phase HEAs requires overcoming thermodynamic barriers; characterization is challenging due to increased compositional and structural complexities; phase segregation can occur if entropy is insufficient to overcome enthalpic differences.. Future work: Further elucidation of structure-property relationships across different HEM subcategories; development of high-throughput synthesis and measurement tools for accelerated materials discovery; deeper mechanistic studies on surface restructuring under reaction conditions; optimization of catalyst stability for noble metal-free applications.. Quote: "The ability to confine multiple principal elements in a single lattice is intriguing for the design of advanced catalysts with desirable activity, selectivity, and stability."

Paper card. Question: How can the configurational entropy in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) be leveraged to overcome the miscibility limitations of traditional alloys and enhance catalytic performance for complex reactions like ethanol oxidation?. System: Platinum-group metal (PGM) high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles containing Ru, Rh, Pd, Os, Ir, and Pt; specifically compared against physical mixtures of unary PGMs and binary/ternary/quaternary/quinary PGM alloys.. Processing: Prepared using a facile polyol method to synthesize PGM-HEA nanoparticles.. Test conditions: Electrochemical ethanol oxidation reaction in aqueous solution; performance compared against commercial Pd/C, Pd black, Pt/C, and Au@PtIr/C catalysts; cyclic voltammetry used to analyze individual constituent contributions.. Findings: The PGM-HEA nanoparticles exhibited much higher activity relative to commercial Pd/C, Pd black, and Pt/C catalysts.; Negligible activity was observed for the physical mixture of the six unary PGM nanoparticles, confirming the necessity of atomic mixing.; The PGM-HEA delivered a mass activity more than 1.5 times higher than that of the most active catalyst to date (Au@PtIr/C).; The PGM-HEA exhibited the highest current density in the full potential range compared to ternary, quaternary, and quinary PGM alloys.; Pt and Pd are active for ethanol conversion but become poisoned by adsorbed (CO)ad or CHx species.; Os and Ru facilitate the oxidation of (CO)ad, mitigating the poisoning effect for Pt and Pd.; Ir and Ru ensure that dehydrogenation or C─C cleavage occurs at a low potential, while further oxidation hinges on Pt and Pd components.. Mechanism: The atomically mixed metals in HEAs play distinct yet concerted functions: Pt and Pd drive ethanol conversion; Os and Ru mitigate poisoning by oxidizing adsorbed species; Ir and Ru lower the potential for C─C cleavage and dehydrogenation. This synergy allows for efficient and complete oxidation of ethanol involving multiple proton-electron transfers.. Limitations: The text notes that while simple reactions can be triggered by mono- and bimetallic PGMs, it is difficult to drive complex reactions involving multiple proton-electron transfers and intermediate species without the synergistic effects provided by HEAs.. Future work: The authors imply the need to better understand the contribution of each metal to the overall reaction, as demonstrated by their comparison of cyclic voltammetry curves of individual constituents to elucidate specific roles in preventing poisoning and facilitating cleavage.. Quote: "The PGM-HEA nanoparticles efficiently catalyzed the ethanol oxidation reaction, exhibiting a much higher activity relative to that of the commercial Pd/C, Pd black, and Pt/C catalysts, respectively."

card: Paper card. Question: How can high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles be synthesized at low temperatures on conventional supports, and what mechanisms govern their formation and catalytic performance in CO2 hydrogenation?. System: CoNiCuRuPd high-entropy alloy nanoparticles supported on TiO2 (CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2); comparison with CoNiCuRuPd/Al2O3, CoNiCuRuPd/MgO, and monometallic Pd/TiO2, Ru/TiO2, Co/TiO2, Ni/TiO2, Cu/TiO2. Processing: Simple impregnation of TiO2 with aqueous solutions of Co(NO3)2·6H2O, Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, Cu(NO3)2·3H2O, RuCl3·nH2O, and Na2PdCl4 (1:1:1:1:1 molar ratio; Pd 1.0 wt%); reduction under H2 flow (20 mL/min) at 400 °C for 2 h without prior calcination. Test conditions: CO2 hydrogenation at atmospheric pressure, 300–400 °C, with N2/H2/CO2 mixture (4/5/1 composition, total flow 50 mL/min, SV = 6000 mL/g/h); stability tested over 72 h; in situ XAFS and XRD under H2 at 200–400 °C; H2-TPR from 50 to 600 °C at 5 °C/min; CO-TPD and FTIR; TEM/STEM/EDX; ETEM under 300 kV electron beam; DFT and MD simulations at 900 K. Findings: CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2 nanoparticles achieved an average size of 1.90 nm with a single-phase fcc structure (lattice parameter a = 3.734 Å), whereas CoNiCuRuPd/Al2O3 and CoNiCuRuPd/MgO yielded larger (6.65 and 6.73 nm), partially segregated particles.; The quinary-component precursors on TiO2 showed a single H2-TPR reduction peak at ~170 °C, indicating simultaneous reduction of all five metal ions, unlike broad peaks (130–250 °C) on Al2O3 and MgO.; CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2 exhibited 2–13 times higher yield of hydrogenated products than MgO and Al2O3 supports, with 68.3% CH4 selectivity at 400 °C.; The apparent activation energy for CO2 hydrogenation on CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2 was 37.7 kJ/mol, lower than 44.2 kJ/mol for Pd/TiO2.; After 72 h of reaction, CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2 retained 96% of its initial activity, while Pd/TiO2 dropped to 76% and Ru/TiO2 to 89%.; Particle growth was suppressed in CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2 (final diameter 2.3 nm) compared to Pd/TiO2 (final diameter 5.3 nm) after 72 h.; DFT calculations showed the cohesive energy of the HEA cluster (−3.92 eV) was higher than that of a pure Pd cluster (−3.09 eV), and diffusion coefficients in the HEA were ~1/3 lower than in pure Pd at 900 K.; CO adsorption on the HEA surface was stronger (Ead = −37.5 kcal/mol) than on pure Pd (−26.2 kcal/mol), shifting the CO stretching frequency from 2091 cm−1 (Pd/TiO2) to 2070 cm−1 (HEA/TiO2) and delaying desorption to >150 °C.. Mechanism: The formation is driven by hydrogen spillover on TiO2: Pd2+ precursors are first reduced to form Pd nuclei; H2 dissociates on Pd to form Pd–H species; protons and electrons transfer to TiO2 lattice O2− anions, generating mobile H atoms that migrate rapidly over TiO2 via coupled proton/electron transfer, reducing all metal precursors simultaneously to form a solid-solution HEA. The sluggish diffusion and lattice distortion in the HEA enhance durability, while the cocktail effect (synergistic electronic properties) improves catalytic activity and CH4 selectivity by strengthening CO adsorption.. Limitations: The study notes that the synthesis method was demonstrated only for the CoNiCuRuPd system and a few preliminary tests with Rh, Pt, and Au; applicability to other compositions requires further investigation. The text also mentions that monometallic Ru/TiO2 showed high activity but attributed it to extremely small particle size (0.89 nm), implying size effects must be controlled when comparing HEAs to monometallics.. Future work: The authors state that 'Further investigation to demonstrate the applicability of the present synthetic method is now under investigation' for other metal combinations (e.g., Rh, Pt, Au) and suggest the approach offers 'advanced insights into an innovative catalyst/photocatalyst architecture providing an essentially unlimited compositional space.'. Quote: "This process is driven by the pronounced hydrogen spillover effect on TiO2 in conjunction with coupled proton/electron transfer."

card: Paper card. Question: Can a CoCrMoNbTi high-entropy alloy be produced using solid-state processing for biomedical applications?. System: CoCrMoNbTi high-entropy alloy. Processing: mechanical alloying in a planetary ball mill. Findings: 1. The alloying degree evaluation was obtained by microstructure analyses, which revealed that the optimal milling time was obtained at 30 h, with a high alloying degree and no contamination.; 2. The results of the mapping analyses presented a good distribution of the elemental metallic powders.; 3. The results of the SEM analyses presented particles with an increased uniformity in size and shape, where the elemental materials were agglomerated and were not separated.; 4. The average particle size for the CoCrMoNbTi high-entropy alloy was determined and a value of 45.12 µm was found, indicating a size reduction of the raw Co and Nb metallic powders during processing.; 5. X-ray diffraction analyses confirmed the theory and indicated that the dual BCC1 and BCC2 phases with the highest intensity were identified as a BCC1 structure, and were preferentially oriented on the (110) plan and minor tetragonal structures.; 6. The TVC phase was identified along the dual BCC phases, indicating the possibility of FCC phases being present in the structure and increased ductility of the studied material.. Mechanism: The high-entropy effect, slow diffusion effect, lattice disorder effect and cocktails effect are responsible for the unique properties of high-entropy alloys.. Future work: The future work will be directed toward the metallic powder consolidation in order to mechanically test the bulk of the final material, but also to obtain electrospark deposition electrodes.. card: Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy alloys (HEAs) be designed to have excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility for medical implants?. System: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) with various compositions, such as TiZrNbTa, HfNbTaTiZr, and TiZrHfNbTa. Test conditions: Tensile and compressive tests, fatigue tests, corrosion tests, and biocompatibility tests. Findings: The equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr achieves a tensile yield strength of 974 MPa and has an elongation of 20%; The O element doped TiZrHfNb exhibited a yield strength of 1,300 MPa and an elongation of 30% in the room temperature tensile test; HfNbTaTiZr exhibits good performance in fatigue tests, with a maximum stress required to exceed the yield stress causing fatigue failure; TiNbTaZrMo HEA exhibited excellent biocompatibility, with osteoblast density higher than that of SUS316L and CP-Ti; TiZrHfNbTa HEA has a corrosion rate of 10–4 mm/year under an environment of a low passive current density of approximately 10–2 A/m2. Mechanism: The excellent mechanical properties of HEAs are attributed to their unique composition and homogeneous microstructure, which leads to a variety of ingredients and complex microstructures. Limitations: The current research on bio-HEAs focuses on in vitro cell viability tests, lacking relevant in vivo animal experiments. card: Paper card. Question: Can CoCrFeNiMo0.85 high-entropy alloy coatings, produced via mechanical alloying and electro spark deposition, provide effective corrosion resistance and adhesion for stainless steel substrates in aggressive geothermal environments?. System: CoCrFeNiMo0.85 high-entropy alloy deposited on 316 L stainless steel substrate. Processing: Solid-state processing: Mechanical alloying of high-purity Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, Mo powders for 30 h in a Pulverisette 6 Classic Line planetary ball mill (350 RPM, ball-to-powder ratio 10:1, N-Heptane process control agent) under Argon; cold pressing at 250 kN into 25 mm × 5 mm samples; sintering at 1100 °C for 1 h; machining into electrodes; electro spark deposition (ESD) under Argon atmosphere to deposit successive layers.. Test conditions: Pull-off testing per ASTM D4541–01; electrochemical corrosion testing in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 25 ± 0.5 °C for 6 h using potentiodynamic polarization.. Findings: Maximum adhesion resistance reached 0.67 MPa, limited by epoxy resin failure rather than coating-substrate interface failure.; Corrosion rate of the ESD coating calculated at 0.00016 mm/year in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution.; Polarization resistance of the coating was higher than 316 L stainless steel (22.50 kΩ × cm2).; XRD analysis revealed an increase in σ phase (rich in Co, Cr, Fe) and μ phase (rich in Mo) in the coating compared to the sintered electrode.; The coating microstructure showed a homogeneous and adhesive layer near the substrate, with slight porosity and splats in the upper part.; After corrosion testing, a passivation layer formed on the surface, covering most pores, containing an oxygen component likely from segregated chromium.; The open circuit potential (Eoc) was more electronegative than the bulk as-cast alloy, attributed to increased porosity delaying passivation.. Mechanism: The authors attribute the phase transformation (increase in σ and μ phases) to the rapid melting and cooling during the electro spark deposition process, driven by temperature differences and local solute solidification. The superior corrosion resistance is explained by the rapid formation of a passivation film, likely containing segregated chromium, which covers surface pores and reduces the corrosion current density significantly compared to bulk alloys or stainless steel.. Limitations: The coating is slightly porous in the upper part due to the BCC structure prone to pore formation in this high-entropy alloy and the ESD technique; the open circuit potential is more electronegative than the bulk alloy due to this porosity delaying passivation.. Future work: The authors state that novel promising coatings resistant to long-term high-temperature oxidation, corrosion action, and wear are currently being sought, implying further development is needed for these specific conditions..
